reviewedControls.readiness: The private worker derives representation, adapter presence and row-worker budget from its loaded engine; it rejects unexpected adapter identity. Readiness binds the selected model and template, pinned adapter SHA-256, context, seed, effective worker budget and supported 0..2 range. Runner strictly validates the corresponding fields, including row-workers on 0.1.13. This reports supported scales, not a per-request applied-scale acknowledgement.
reviewedControls.canonicalCountGeneration: The private service strictly canonicalizes the selected profile, allowing exactly pinned adapter slot 0 with a finite f64 scale in 0..2. Count clears any older prepared input, seals exact canonical bytes and the session-owned f32 adapter scale, and retains the prepared request only after acknowledgement. Generate consumes that one prepared request and compares its exact canonical body against the requested body before model execution. Duplicate, overridden or unknown fields and a changed scale reject. Signed zero remains distinguishable in the f64 canonical bytes.
reviewedControls.freshGraphState: SwiftSession prepares the selected scale under Runtime::prepare_profile_request. With the serving default PromptReuse::Disabled, every request resets the complete graph state and checkpoint provenance; scale changes, including signed zero and change-back, cannot reuse earlier state. Successful graph reset clears committed tokens, logits and saved checkpoints. This source property is distinct from captured full-model numerical-state equality.
reviewedControls.samplerBoundary: Runtime profile reset deliberately leaves caller-owned sampler draws unchanged. SwiftSession::reset and a fresh owner restore the initial seeded sampler. Equal visible same-owner output alone therefore does not prove sampler reset, exact full-state restoration or absence of stale state.
reviewedControls.cancellationAndSettlement: Dropping a private exchange future cancels the shared request; failed delivery also cancels. Output uses a bounded one-event acknowledged lane. The private service waits for the active worker to settle before a following request. Failure after generation starts faults admission, and unsuccessful terminal acknowledgement cannot be relabelled successful completion. Worker Drop cancels and joins the model thread; the externally owned Job remains the hard termination boundary.
reviewedControls.privateReset: Authenticated private Reset clears the retained counted input, faults admission during reset and only reopens it after engine reset and acknowledgement. A pre-reset counted request cannot be generated afterward. This private administrative route is not part of Runner's public chat contract; a public replay must not be described as having called it.

regressionScope: Source review of exact released regression implementations, including fake-engine negative controls; no local tests or new test-execution claim. These complement actual-model service observations and do not turn a fake engine into numerical model evidence.

needsActualModel: Exact released service/worker readiness for current-weight PTQ1, pinned adapter and four workers under unchanged ownership and memory admission.
Bound terminal streams at 1.3, negative zero and 2.0, with exact request identities and invalid-scale/context rejection.
A bounded content-bearing request abandoned before terminal framing, owned teardown and a fresh owner replay at 1.3.
Power observations before and after the workload, immutable source/hosted-binary identities and cleanup receipts within one original aggregate owner clock.
sourceEvidenceRemainsSeparate: Public invalid-scale rejection happens before private counting; it does not itself exercise stale private count/generate bytes.
Fresh-owner replay observes a clean process and seeded sampler, not retained-graph rollback state equality.
Retained original-PQ2 rollback has its own exact historical device identity and requires independent applicability review for later Runner source.

independentPrerequisites: Immutable approved-adapter authoring checkpoint/conversion/direction inputs and authentic all-48 SSM writer-basis provenance cannot be supplied by native/Rust agreement or this source review.
Human quality/creative/comfort acceptance and a clean-machine installation cannot be supplied by a model-free source audit.

Full 8192-token scalar/NEON state trajectories and 4096 output tokens cannot be inferred from cap-one streams; if they cannot fit the owner budget they remain pending for an appropriate independent CI environment.

Power-matched paired benefit must retain losing outcomes and meet the unchanged latency or accepted capacity/energy criterion; known equal endpoint snapshots alone do not establish uninterrupted stability.
